scope: Incremental applicability/calibration only; primary statements and [INFERENCE] transfers kept separate; no correctness replays or novelty promotion.

output.summary: This is a bounded, read-only audit of the delta, run 2026-10-19. Correctness was not rechecked. I read 5 new primary sources (limit 8) and re-read the pinned sections of SC2007, SC2008, GLYZ, the Chen–Savchev slides and the ZY2011 summary. Item by item: (1) CT follows immediately from DeVos–Goddyn–Mohar (DGM) Corollary 1.5 at G=C_p. DGM's own text states the complement-shift identity Σ_{m−ℓ}=σ−Σ_ℓ that CT uses. CTgen is CT plus pigeonhole plus even deletion of the involution. This is the H={0} case of the argument in GLYZ Lemma 6, whose statement is vacuous at C_p. Neither lemma deserves credit. (2) LS+2 assembles classical statements in a routine way: DGM, SC2007 Thm 7/8 and Prop 5, and elementary CF arithmetic. Its SLZ3 step can be replaced by LS(p,p−2) [INFERENCE]. (3) LS-lin transfers the proof method of SC2008 Thm 5 step by step; it is not a corollary of any statement. The transferred pieces are the maximal zero subsequence, the SC2007-normalized zero-free remainder, Prop 3(b) length control, the first-crossing observation/(3), and the Prop 4(a) exclusion. Only Step 5, which pins the multiplier a=−1, has no SC2008 analogue. It is needed because (ZP_κ) is not translation-invariant in x-coordinates (equivalently, not dilation-invariant in CF coordinates). That step, together with (6b), sets the bound p≥6e−10, while the classical inputs already hold for p≥4e−3. (4) The BASE1 classification remains corollary-level given Zeng–Yuan 2011 (summary only; the full text still returns 403). BASE1+ still needs SLZ3. (5) New reduction [INFERENCE]: after the EGZ split X=Y−A, take SC2008's normal form uX+t=α∪β. If t∈{0,1/2}, a Prop 4(a)-type count rules out every odd zero-sum of length ≥p+2. CF multipliers correspond to translations: a=−1↔t=1/2, a=−1/2↔t=0, E2↔t=3/2, E3↔t=−1/2. So the exact missing lemma is translation/multiplier pinning. It is needed for the remaining LS cells with p≥4e−3 and for LS+ cells with p≥6e−5. (6) If the unreviewed LS+-lin (p≥10e−13) is correct, it gives a sharp LS+ band, attained by E2/E3. It does not improve any located published bound under matched assumptions. It adds no LS cell, does not cover STAB, and stays inside the classical-tool frontier p>6e−6. (7) Two of the four smallest open LS cells, (17,12) and (23,16), are p≡2 mod 3 base cells with κ=(2p+2)/3. There a shortest long zero-sum has length 2p+2 and factors into 2 or 3 atoms, so ZY2011 (k=2, plus its unread k≥3 extension) is the natural classical route. The Chen–Savchev 'shorter long' theorem was published in J. Number Theory 177 (2017). GLYZ Thms 3/11 require p≥53. Nothing here is major and no novelty is claimed. LS, LS+, STAB and ordered Olson remain open.

findings.claim: CT follows immediately from DGM Cor. 1.5 at G=C_p. If σ_p(Y)∉Σ_n(A), then Σ_n(A)≠C_p, so H=stab(Σ_n(A)) is trivial and p−1≥1−n+Σ_x min(n,v_x). The 3-line reduction is in theorem_comparison.precise_reductions R1 [INFERENCE; DGM statement verified].
findings.quote: If a = (a1, a2,..., am) is a sequence of elements of G, ℓ ≤ m, and H = stab(Σℓ(a)), then |Σℓ(a)| ≥ |H|(1 − ℓ + Σ_{Q∈G/H} min{ℓ, #{i ∈ {1,..., m} : ai ∈ Q}}).
findings.source: M. DeVos, L. Goddyn, B. Mohar, A generalization of Kneser's Addition Theorem, Adv. Math. 220 (2009) 1531-1548, Corollary 1.5
findings.date_version: IMFM Ljubljana preprint series Vol. 45 (2007) 1032, dated March 16/23, 2007 (author-hosted); journal version not read
findings.verified: true (pp. 1-4 read: abstract, Thm 1.3, Cor 1.5 and the complement remark; ℓ glyphs lost in extraction were restored from context)
findings.scope: Any abelian G; applied with G=C_p to the C_p-coordinates of Y
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: NEW primary read. Earlier screens knew DGM only through GLYZ Lemma 5, and the credit addendum called CT 'DGM type'.

findings.claim: DGM itself states the complement-shift identity that CT uses: an n-term subsequence with sum σ(Y) corresponds to a zero-sum complement of length |Y|−n. So at G=C_p, CT adds nothing beyond DGM.
findings.quote: Note that if a = (a1,..., am) and ℓ ≤ m, then it follows immediately that Σ_{m−ℓ}(a) = (Σ ai) − Σℓ(a). Thus, the sets Σ_{m−ℓ}(a) and −Σℓ(a) are shifts of one another

findings.claim: The proof of GLYZ Lemma 6 is the published template for CTgen. With no |G|-term zero-sum, the complement identity and DGM force a value of multiplicity ≥ℓ+1 when H={0}. CTgen is the C_p analogue with a window length, plus even deletion of the involution [proof-method transfer, INFERENCE]. The Lemma 6 statement itself needs ℓ≥|G|/p+p−2. At G=C_p that means length ≥2p−1, where EGZ already applies, so the statement is vacuous there.
findings.quote: Assume to the contrary that 0 ∉ Σn(S). Then, |Σn(S)| ≤ n − 1. Since Σℓ(S) = σ(S) − Σn(S), we have |Σℓ(S)| = |Σn(S)| ≤ n − 1.
findings.source: W. Gao, Y. Li, P. Yuan, J. Zhuang, Arch. Math. 105 (2015) 361-370, proof of Lemma 6
findings.date_version: author preprint dated 2015-05-07 (previously pinned); journal version not read
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: NEW use. Earlier screens cited only GLYZ Lemma 5 and Cor 9.

findings.claim: SC2008's proof of Thm 5 splits the sequence into a maximum zero subsequence σ and a zero-free remainder τ. LS-lin Step 3 does the same in CF coordinates: Z0 is an inclusion-maximal mod-p zero-sum and U'=U−Z0 is zero-sum-free. LS+-RED (B) and its addenda do likewise [mapping INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Select a zero subsequence σ of γ with nonzero terms and of maximum length; σ may be the empty sequence. This choice implies that the remaining nonzero terms of γ form a zero-free sequence τ.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, Long n-zero-free sequences in finite cyclic groups, Discrete Math. 308 (2008) 1-8, proof of Thm 5
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: NEW mapping. Earlier screens mapped only FB to SC2008 (3) and LS-lin Step 4 to SC2007.

findings.claim: SC2008 can normalize freely because n-term zero sums survive both translation and multiplication by a unit. In x-coordinates, (ZP_κ) survives multiplication but not translation. Since CF coordinates are an affine image of x-coordinates, a μ-dilation is an x-affine map, so LS-lin must pin a=−1 (Step 5, no-wrap p≥6e−10). This is the only LS-lin step without an SC2008 counterpart. Together with (6b) it is the sole source of the band limit [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Translations in Z_n do not affect sums of length n ... We multiply by the same integer all remaining terms of γ, which preserves the zero sums of any length.
findings.scope: Identifies the non-transferable step and the origin of the 6e−10 (LS) and 9e−13 (LS+-RED) limits

findings.claim: SC2008 Prop 3(b) (subsequence sums with length control) is the source of LS-lin Step 4's rule that an x-sum s needs at least s−E' terms. It is also the source of the first-crossing estimates in Step 6, which replace SC2008's maximality 'observation' and inequality (3) by (F*) [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: each integer in the interval [2ℓ − S, S] is representable as the sum of a subsequence of α with length at least 2ℓ − S.
findings.scope: LS-lin Steps 4 and 6; LS+-RED addenda Steps 1-3

findings.claim: SC2008 Prop 4(a) is the pattern behind the exclusion steps: LS-lin Step 7, LS+2 (E) and the addenda's Step 4. New [INFERENCE] variant R5: with the normal form of X=Y−A, a translation t≡1/2 rules out every odd zero-sum of length ≥p in X by the same count (target residue (m−p)/2), and t≡0 does so by Prop 4(a) verbatim.
findings.quote: Therefore r ≤ Σ a_i = Σ −b_j < n − |β|, implying r + |β| < n. Since |γ| ≤ r + |β|, we infer that α ∪ β is n-zero-free.
findings.verified: true for the quote; R5 is a hand derivation [INFERENCE]
findings.scope: Exclusion half of LS/LS+ once the translation or multiplier is pinned
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: Quote previously pinned. The R5 extension to t=1/2 and the a↔t dictionary are NEW.

findings.claim: SC2008 Prop 4(c) (two heavy values with combined multiplicity ≥2k) is the classical form of the two-heavy-value structure. That structure appears in LS+2 Step 1 (one value ≥2p−2, or two values ≥p−1) and in LS+-RED case (β) [analogy, INFERENCE].
findings.quote: The multiplicities u and v of 1 and 0 in α ∪ β satisfy u + v ≥ 2k, max(u, v) ≥ k, min(u, v) ≥ 2k − n + 1.

findings.claim: SC2007 Thm 7: the normalizer is one of the sequence's own terms. LS+2 Step 3 (B)-(C), LS-lin Step 4 and LS+-RED (B) use exactly SC2007 Thm 7/8 and Prop 5 as statements, applied to cores of length >p/2.
findings.quote: Each zero-free sequence of length greater than n/2 in the cyclic group Z_n is behaving with respect to one of its terms.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, Long zero-free sequences in finite cyclic groups, Discrete Math. 307 (2007) 2671-2679, Thm 7
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: The Thm 7 quote is new. Identification for LS+2 and LS+-RED is NEW; v3 had it only for I-small and LS-lin Step 4.

findings.claim: The index-one threshold ⌊n/2⌋+2 is tight. So the core-length conditions p≥4e−3 (LS) and p≥6e−5 (LS+) are genuine classical barriers for the SC2007 route. Cells below them need 2-element-basis input.
findings.quote: These modifications of the examples at the end of the previous section show that the upper bound ℓ(Z_n) ≤ ⌊n/2⌋ + 2 is tight for even n ≥ 6 and odd n ≥ 9.
findings.scope: Sub-band B of the remaining LS cells (e.g. (23,16))
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: NEW. v3 cited SC2008's optimality examples, not SC2007's tightness.

findings.claim: GLYZ Thm 3 (n odd ≥50, zero-free length in (⌊n/3⌋+1, ⌊n/2⌋]) gives a near-index-one normal form after removing at most 2 terms. It is the published replacement of SC2007 Thm 8 for short cores. Its n≥50 hypothesis excludes all four smallest open cells (p≤23).
findings.quote: Then, by removing at most two elements from S, the remaining sequence is equivalent to a sequence whose index is not more than 1 − 4/n.
findings.scope: Tool for LS cells with p≤4e−4 and p≥53; no implication
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: v3 named it as a tool. The precise role and the p≥53 exclusion of the small cells are NEW.

findings.claim: GLYZ Thm 11 (positive-integer sequences of length t>(n+2)/3 with σ<n and 1∈S) shows subset sums are an interval up to one exceptional term. It is the published replacement of SC2007 Prop 5 ('behaving') below n/2, so it would carry LS-lin's greedy step to shorter cores.
findings.quote: If 1 ∈ S, then Σ(S) is an interval except for the case when S = S0 n_l, where Σ(S0) is an interval and n_l > σ(S0) + 1.

findings.claim: The Chen–Savchev 'shorter long' characterization was published. Earlier screens had it only as slides or a 'manuscript'. With slide Thm 4 it gives a 1- or 2-element basis for minimal zero-sum sequences of length in [⌊n/3⌋+3, ⌊n/2⌋+1], n≥10. That length range is exactly where U'(−σ(U')) falls for LS cells with p≤4e−4.
findings.quote: The article characterizes the minimal zero-sum sequences over the cyclic group C_n with lengths between ⌊n/3⌋+3 and ⌊n/2⌋+1, for n ≥ 10.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, An inverse problem about minimal zero-sum sequences over finite cyclic groups, J. Number Theory 177 (2017) 381-427, DOI 10.1016/j.jnt.2017.01.001
findings.date_version: zbMATH Open publisher summary, read 2026-10-19; full text not read
findings.verified: true (summary only; the 1-/2-element-basis wording comes from the pinned CANT 2016 slides, Thm 4)
findings.scope: Tool for sub-band B, e.g. (23,16); no implication
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: NEW: resolves the earlier access hole ('SC2017 (JNT) not read'; 'publication not checked').

findings.claim: Published structure results on unsplittable sequences cover lengths ≥⌊n/3⌋+8 (large n whose least prime divisor is >13, so large primes qualify). Zeng–Yuan–Li treat lengths [⌊n/3⌋+3, ⌊n/2⌋+1] for odd n>50 (Acta Arith. 176 (2016) 131-159, per the JNT 2017 reference list). These are further inputs for short cores; not read.
findings.quote: Recently Yuan and Li [5] solved the same problem for length ≥ ⌊n/3⌋+8, for sufficiently large n with least prime divisor greater than 13.
findings.source: F. Chen (with S. Savchev), CANT 2016 slides, p. 8; [5] = Yuan-Li, Int. J. Number Theory 12 (2016) 979-993
findings.verified: true for the slide text; the cited papers were not read

findings.claim: Hypotheses of ZY2011 at summary level: g∈G is not stated to be a generator, n_i∈[1,n], Σn_i=2n. For an odd T over C_2p, g must be an odd generator. Even elements give even terms. The involution g=p would make T=p^(2p+2), which contains p^(2κ+2), a zero-sum of window length forbidden by (ZP_κ). So v3's BASE1 route stands [INFERENCE]. For BASE1+ the result does not replace SLZ3. A shortest long zero-sum of length >3κ is a 2-atom product, so ZY2011 applies to it, but excluding it still needs SLZ3's counting.
findings.quote: Then there exists some g ∈ G such that S = (n1g)·(n2g)·…·(n|S|g), where ni ∈ [1, n] for all i ∈ [1, |S|] and n1 + n2 + … + n|S| = 2n.
findings.source: X. Zeng, P. Yuan, Indexes of long zero-sum sequences over cyclic groups, Eur. J. Combin. 32 (2011) 1213-1221
findings.verified: true (summary only; full text returned HTTP 403)
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: Quote previously pinned. The generator/involution hypothesis check and the BASE1+ non-implication argument are NEW.

findings.claim: ZY2011 also treats products of k≥3 atoms (statement not visible). This matters for the base cells with p≡2 mod 3 and κ=(2p+2)/3, which include the open LS cells (17,12) and (23,16). There SLZ3 gives a shortest long zero-sum T of length 3κ=2p+2. Every proper zero-sum of T has length in [κ,2κ], so T is a product of 2 atoms, or of 3 atoms each of length κ. This is exactly where BASE1's S2 fails. ZY2011 k=2 plus its k≥3 extension is therefore the natural classical route to a 'BASE2' classification [INFERENCE; not executed].
findings.quote: And we also generalize the above result to long zero-sum sequences which can be decomposed into at most k ≥ 3 minimal zero-sum sequences.
findings.verified: true (summary sentence only; the k≥3 hypotheses are unknown)
findings.scope: BASE2 cells; strongest classical route for 2 of the 4 smallest open LS cells

findings.claim: SC2008 Thm 5 applied after the EGZ split gives a normal form for X=Y−A exactly when p>4e−4 (LS, |X|=2p−2e+1) or p>6e−6 (LS+, |X|=2p−3e+2). The SC2007 core thresholds are the same: p≥4e−3 and p≥6e−5. The normal form holds only up to affine similarity, so the translation t is the residual datum [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: A sequence of length greater than 3n/2−1 in the cyclic group Z_n does not contain an n-term zero subsequence if and only if it is similar to the union of two sequences α and β
findings.scope: Classical frontier for LS and LS+
findings.new_vs_previous_screen: The LS frontier (4e−4) was in v3. The LS+ frontier (6e−6), the coincidence with the core thresholds, and t as the exact residual are NEW.

findings.claim: The closest published pattern to LS+-type statements is an exact constrained extremal length derived quickly from a normal-form theorem inside its range: g(n,k) in SC2008 §5, and h(n,k) in SC2007 §8. The constraints differ and there is no matched comparator for the window/coset problem.
findings.quote: For positive integers n and k, k ≤ n, let g(n, k) ≥ k be the least integer such that each sequence in Z_n with at least k distinct terms and length g(n, k) contains an n-term zero sum.

theorem_comparison.setting: Odd elements of C_2p are the elements (1,x) of C_2×C_p. A subsequence of length m is a zero-sum iff m is even and its x-sum is 0. (ZP_κ) forbids x-zero-sums of even length in [2κ+2,2p]. Put e=p−κ. CF coordinates relative to an odd generator g are μ=(c−1)/2 for the element cg, i.e. μ=x/(2x_g)−1/2, an affine image of x.
delta_statements_exact: LS-lin (verdict item 5): p prime, κ0+1≤κ≤p−2, e≥3, p≥6e−10 ⇒ LS(p,κ). With e=2 the band is e≤(p+10)/6.
LS+2 (item 4): κ=p−2, p≥7. An odd (ZP_κ) Y with a zero-sum of length ≥2p+2 has |Y|≤3p−5=3κ+1; E2/E3 attain the bound.
BASE1/BASE1+ (item 3): p≡1 mod 3, p≥7, κ=(2p+1)/3. Such a Y of length 2p+2 is E2 or E3; every such Y has length ≤2p+2.
CT (item 6): Σ_x min(n,v_x(Y))≤p+n−2 whenever |Y|−n is even and lies in [2κ+2,2p]. CTgen (item 7): (p−3)/2≤κ≤p−1, N≥2κ+3, Y has a long zero-sum ⇒ v_involution≤N−2κ−2 and some generator has v≥N−2κ−1.
LS+-lin (CANDIDATE_UNVERIFIED): e=2, or e≥3 and p≥10e−13 ⇒ LS+(p,κ).

precise_reductions.name: R1 CT from DGM
precise_reductions.derivation: Let A be the C_p-coordinates of Y. For S⊂Y with |S|=n, the complement Y−S has even length m=|Y|−n in the window, and it is a zero-sum iff σ_p(S)=σ_p(Y). So (ZP_κ) gives σ_p(Y)∉Σ_n(A), hence Σ_n(A)≠C_p. Σ_n(A) is nonempty (n≤|Y|) and a union of H-cosets, so H={0}. DGM Cor 1.5 then gives p−1≥1−n+Σ_x min(n,v_x).

precise_reductions.name: R2 CTgen
precise_reductions.derivation: Put n=N−2κ−2≥1. CT gives Σ min(n,v_x)≤p+n−2<N, since κ≥(p−3)/2, so some v_x≥n+1. If the involution had v_p≥n+1, a long zero-sum T would contain ≥|T|−2κ−1 copies of it. Deleting |T|−2p of them (an even number ≥2) leaves a zero-sum of length 2p, which is forbidden.

precise_reductions.name: R3 LS+2
precise_reductions.derivation: If |Y|≥3p−3=p+2κ+1, LS(p,p−2) gives (S1), so there is no long zero-sum. That leaves |Y|=3p−4, where the lane's Steps 1-3 run: DGM/CT with n=p−2; CF coordinates; a zero-free core of length ≥p−3>p/2; SC2007 Thm 7/8 and Prop 5; a^(−1)∈{−1,−2}; then the Prop 4(a)-type count.

precise_reductions.name: R4 LS-lin ↔ SC2008
map: Step 1 (DGM-p dominant g at μ=0) ↔ translating so that 0 has maximum multiplicity (+ Prop 2)
Step 3 (Z0 maximal, U' zero-free) ↔ σ maximal, τ zero-free
Step 4 (index one + greedy, needs p≥4e−3) ↔ Theorem 1 (=SC2007 Thm 8) on τ + Prop 3(b)
Step 6 (first-crossing via (F*)) ↔ the 'observation' n−v_j>S and the minimal crossing behind (3)

precise_reductions.name: R5 exclusion after the EGZ split
precise_reductions.derivation: uX+t=α∪β with L(α)

precise_reductions.name: R6 dictionary between multipliers and translations
precise_reductions.statement: If the two heavy values are g (c=1) and w=c_w·g, then up to z↦1−z we have t=c_w/(c_w−1)=(2a+1)/(2a), where a=μ_w. So a=−1↔t=1/2, a=−1/2 (involution)↔t=0, a=1 (E2)↔t=3/2 and a=−1/3 (E3)↔t=−1/2. Checked by hand on E2: A=h^p and T−A=h^3(3h)^(p−1) has z-sum 3≡(p+2)·3/2.
precise_reductions.status: [INFERENCE]; it assumes the heavy values persist in X

precise_reductions.name: R7 BASE1 via ZY2011
precise_reductions.derivation: v3's derivation, unchanged. g is forced to be an odd generator (orders in C_2p and parity); g=p is excluded because p^(2κ+2) would be a forbidden zero-sum.

precise_reductions.name: R8 BASE2 cells
precise_reductions.derivation: κ=(2p+2)/3 with p≡2 mod 3. SLZ3 gives a shortest long zero-sum T with |T|=3κ=2p+2. Proper zero-sums have length in [κ,2κ], so T has 2 atoms, or 3 atoms of length κ each. Classifying T and proving 2-term non-extension would give LS+ there, hence LS at (17,12), (23,16), (29,20), ...

classical_frontiers.LS: Classical inputs (SC2007 on the core, or SC2008 on X) hold for p≥4e−3. LS-lin covers p≥6e−10. Sub-band A of the open cells (classical inputs available, pinning missing): (17,12), (19,14), (23,17). Sub-band B (core ≤p/2): (23,16).
classical_frontiers.LS_plus: Classical inputs hold for p≥6e−5 (SC2008 split: p>6e−6). LS+-RED needs p≥9e−13 and addendum 2 needs p≥10e−16. Gap cells where classical inputs apply but LS+-lin does not: (13,10), (19,15), (23,19), (29,24), (31,25), (31,26) [hand arithmetic].

missing_hypotheses: SC2008 → LS/LS+: the theorem is affine-invariant, but (ZP_κ) is not translation-invariant. Missing: a lemma pinning t∈{0,1/2,1}; for LS+, also excluding the E-channels t∈{3/2,−1/2} at length 3κ+2.
SC2007 → cores: length >p/2, i.e. p≥4e−3 (LS) or p≥6e−5 (LS+); the bound is tight.
ZY2011 → BASE1+/LS+: it covers T, not Y⊋T. For BASE2 it needs the 3-atom case, whose hypotheses are unread.
GLYZ Thms 3/4: n odd ≥50. Thm 11 presupposes an index<1 normalization with 1∈S.
GLYZ Lemma 6/Thm 8/Cor 9: ℓ≥|G|/p+p−2, vacuous at C_p.
strongest_classical_route: 1. SC2008 §3 (Thm 5 proof, Props 3-4) read with SC2007 Thm 7, applied to X=Y−A. Its hypotheses hold for every open LS cell with p>4e−4 and every LS+ gap cell. What remains is the pinning lemma; R5 then closes in a few lines.
2. For BASE2 cells, including (17,12) and (23,16): ZY2011 k=2 plus its k≥3 extension, applied to a shortest long zero-sum of length 2p+2. The full text is needed.
3. For cores ≤p/2: Savchev-Chen JNT 177 (2017) for n≥10. GLYZ Thms 3/11 only for p≥53. Zeng-Yuan-Li (Acta Arith. 2016) and Yuan-Li (IJNT 2016), unread.

LSplus_lin_matched_assessment.if_correct: A sharp LS+ length bound 3κ+1 (attained by E2/E3) for e=2 and for e≥3 with p≥10e−13; for primes this is equivalent to p≥10e−16.
LSplus_lin_matched_assessment.published_matched_comparator: None identified. The located bounds have weaker hypotheses (3p−2 from s_2p(C_p)) or are different invariants. LS+ is 3e−3 below 3p−2, but only under extra hypotheses, so this is not an improvement under matched assumptions.
LSplus_lin_matched_assessment.relative_to_classical_frontier: It stops at e≲p/10, against e≲p/6 for the classical inputs. The limit comes from lane-specific no-wrap and involution counting, not from any classical hypothesis.
LSplus_lin_matched_assessment.relative_to_LS_lin: Every covered cell lies inside LS-lin's band, so there is no new LS cell. STAB is not covered.
LSplus_lin_matched_assessment.verdict: If correct: modest and sharp, but not a matched quantitative theorem and not major. Correctness was not assessed here.

significance.rubric: 'Major' would require a new method, a solved prominent problem, or a published bound improved under matched assumptions. None is established.
significance.CT_CTgen: No credit: immediate DGM corollaries (primary source verified); GLYZ Lemma 6 is the template.
significance.LS_plus_2: Routine: classical statements plus CF arithmetic [INFERENCE]. Not located verbatim.
significance.LS_lin: Modest specialist result: a transfer of SC2008's proof. Its delta is the window-adapted multiplier pinning plus bookkeeping. The band is limited by the pinning, not by classical hypotheses.
significance.BASE1: Corollary-level given ZY2011 [v3 INFERENCE; summary only]. BASE1+ is modest and relies on the lane's SLZ3.
significance.overall: Not major. No novelty or priority claim. LS, LS+, STAB and ordered Olson remain open.

counterpoints: R4-R8 and the frontier and gap-cell lists are my unreviewed hand derivations. R6 assumes the heavy values persist in X; when the 0/1 multiplicities are small this can fail.
R5 settles only the exclusion half. Pinning may genuinely fail below 6e−10 (wrap-around multipliers), so the classical frontier is not a provable band.
A specialist might find the pinning routine (an AP-in-arc lemma), which would make LS-lin and LS+-lin fully routine. Or the specialist might find it substantive.
ZY2011 and SC2017 are known only at summary level, and the hypotheses of ZY2011's k≥3 extension are unknown. They may not cover |T|=2p+2.
DGM was read as the 2007 preprint and GLYZ as the 2015 preprint; journal numbering or statements could differ.
'No matched comparator' reflects a bounded search. Earlier screens dropped interval-length invariants (Augspurger et al. 2016 and others) without full reads.

new_vs_previous_screens: Read the DGM primary. CT follows directly from DGM Cor 1.5 plus DGM's own complement remark.
GLYZ Lemma 6 is the template for CTgen, and its statement is vacuous at C_p.
Full mapping of LS-lin, LS+2 and LS+-RED onto SC2008's proof. Step 5 is identified as the only non-transferable step and the only limiter of the band.
R5 and the a↔t dictionary: the residual problem along SC2008's route is exactly pinning.
The LS+ classical frontier (6e−6/6e−5) and the gap cells.
Sorting of the open LS cells. (17,12) and (23,16) are BASE2 cells, so ZY2011 k=2/k≥3 is the natural route there.
The shorter-long theorem was published in JNT 2017. GLYZ Thm 11 is the 'behaving' substitute, and GLYZ's p≥53 condition excludes the small cells.
ZY2011 hypothesis check, and the finding that it cannot replace SLZ3.
